song.title: The House Of The Rising Sun

guitar.evidence: Hilton Valentine of The Animals (famous for the arpeggiated intro on 'House of the Rising Sun') is documented using Gretsch and Rickenbacker guitars in the British Invasion era.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with medium confidence.

tone.target: dark clean arpeggio with slight tube grit and room
tone.profile: dark clean arpeggio with slight tube grit and room
tone.summary: A fingerpicked arpeggio tone achieved using a Comp for warmth, followed by a low-gain UK 50/UK Vintage 4x12 setup to provide the required clean edge of breakup and dark, spacious sound.

rig.name: The Animals - The House Of The Rising Sun - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and fingerpicking transients.
Smooth out the dynamics of fingerpicked arpeggios and add warmth.
Provide the required slight edge of breakup and dark grit without sounding aggressive.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general British tone; setting it low provides the desired 'edge' rather than full overdrive.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more aggressive option if the grit needs to be noticeable.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No distortion needed for clean arpeggios).
Simulate the Vox/clean British amp tone required for a dark, clean arpeggio.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if the UK 50 is too bright.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet sound matching the UK 50 amp.
Darken the overall tone and emphasize the minor-key movement.
blocks.gap: The EQ is used subtly to shape the dark, melancholic sound required by the song's mood.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required subtle room ambience without sounding washed out.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the small room ambience and classic British sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the intimate, dark British tone required for arpeggios.
